status: Public baseline 1e5c4fd connects eight Freestyle environments, recovered terrain and vegetation, music, responsive Rust-drawn menus, touch rider input and portrait camera framing. CI 38186584449 and public browser checks passed for that baseline. A newer host candidate passes an actual-content wreck/reset loop and a separate clean touch-ramp landing; its release-specific public check is pending. Crash behavior remains partial, and the train, full race flow, original terrain LOD, and stunt scoring are unfinished.
working_on: Verify the host-tested crash candidate against its exact release and continue native wreck-camera and rider-versus-prop/water work. Then connect the recovered Arlington train and ten-car route.

entries.title: Original terrain recovered
entries.summary: ENV01 terrain renders directly from the locally opened game disc.
details: Recovered the tile hierarchy and elevation data in Rust.
entries.limitation: At this checkpoint the terrain used temporary colors, and there was no riding simulation.
entries.caption: Earlier build: recovered ENV01 terrain with temporary colors.

entries.title: Original ATV and textures
entries.summary: The original ATV mesh and its base textures are visible on the original terrain.
details: Recovered mesh packets, node transforms, texture palettes and material references.
entries.limitation: This was a static model checkpoint. Terrain materials, the rider and gameplay were still missing.
entries.caption: Earlier build: the original ATV, before driving and rider integration.

entries.title: First driving simulation
entries.summary: The ATV now moves through Rust vehicle simulation compiled to WebAssembly.
details: Connected recovered drivetrain, wheel rotation, suspension, terrain contact and body integration.
Browser checks confirmed acceleration, steering and braking.
entries.limitation: This is a partial reconstruction. Track obstacles, crashes, races and original camera behavior remain incomplete.
entries.caption: First browser driving checkpoint, before the original rider was added.

entries.title: Original rider seated on the ATV
entries.summary: The original rider mesh, textures and a sampled original animation pose now move with the vehicle.
details: All 146 original MOT animation files decoded and sampled successfully.
entries.limitation: The visible rider currently uses a sampled seated pose. Gameplay animation selection, blending and hand/foot constraints are not finished.
entries.caption: Original rider at the seated-pose integration checkpoint.

entries.title: Original terrain textures decoded
entries.summary: Snow and rock textures now come from the game instead of temporary terrain colors.
details: The textures use PS2 IPUM compression. A new Rust decoder processes the original payloads in the browser.
596 terrain and sky mip images decoded. Ten YUV comparisons against an independent decoder differed by at most one level.
All 68 ENV01 base textures are mapped through the authored terrain hierarchy.
entries.limitation: Original detail layers, lighting, sky placement and texture seams still need fidelity checks.
entries.caption: Narrow-screen browser capture: original ATV, rider and decoded ENV01 snow textures.

entries.title: Engine audio and handling checks
entries.summary: Original engine samples are connected, and more recovered handling behavior is running in the vehicle simulation.
details: Engine sound transitions matched 1,200 scenarios executed through an instruction interpreter of the original routine.
Wheelie, jump preload, air control, steering slew and dynamic center of mass have been connected.
Browser checks cover driving, braking, reset, controller mapping, simultaneous touch, focus pause and graphics-context recovery.
entries.limitation: These checks do not establish a full match to PS2 gameplay. The original sound mixer, full animation behavior, obstacle response and race systems remain incomplete.

entries.title: Track objects and engine sound in the browser
entries.summary: The scene now includes original track objects at their recovered positions, with original engine samples playing during driving.
details: 174 prop instances, 68 terrain textures and 21 engine samples loaded from the disc.
Verified through the private HTTPS site: driving, braking, reset, controller mapping, touch input, focus pause and graphics-context recovery.
No JavaScript or WebGL errors were recorded in the checkpoint run.
entries.limitation: Some prop materials still use neutral rendering. Reflective ice and one unsupported tower mesh are omitted. Sky, obstacle response, full animation and music are still being connected.
entries.caption: Current browser checkpoint: original terrain, placed track objects, ATV and rider. Engine audio was active in the same run.

entries.title: Original sky and streaming soundtrack
entries.summary: The recovered sky renders above ENV01, and original music streams directly from the locally opened disc.
details: The 21-song catalog is decoded in Rust; browser verification streamed What’s Golden with no underruns during the checkpoint run.
Stereo ADPCM decoding preserves predictors between chunks. A complete track matched the existing full-file decoder sample for sample.
Music uses small scheduled buffers rather than decoding an entire track into memory.
entries.limitation: Music selection uses the recovered shuffle routine with a provisional random seed. Original mixer levels and every playback transition are not yet verified; race systems and full rider animation remain incomplete.
entries.caption: Browser checkpoint with the original sky, track, ATV and rider; original music was streaming during this capture.

entries.title: Public browser build and collision recovery
entries.summary: The game build and screenshot log are now available on public Sites; Tailscale is no longer required.
details: Public HTTPS checks loaded all eight existing log entries and seven screenshots, and streamed original music with no underruns.

Private GitHub Actions now builds the Rust/WASM release and checks code on main. A scheduled publisher is configured to check successful builds every 15 minutes; its first unattended run has not yet been observed.
The recovered chassis contact solver matched 1,400 instruction-interpreter cases; integration with the original collision hull is being verified in the browser.
entries.limitation: The browser build remains incomplete. Original obstacle contact generation, crash behavior, full animations, races and progression are still under reconstruction.

entries.title: Original chassis hull connected
entries.summary: The vehicle now uses its original 34-point chassis hull for terrain contact, alongside the wheel suspension.
details: The ray-tree loader decoded all 38 distinct original type-2 collision files. ATV01 hull traversal matched the original endpoint order bit for bit.
Impact and friction routines matched 1,400 instruction-interpreter cases before browser integration.
Both compressed scene texture containers now decode, removing the remaining unsupported scene-texture fallback.
Real-disc browser checks passed for chassis loading, driving, braking, reset, music, engine sound, controller mapping, simultaneous touch and graphics-context recovery.
entries.limitation: Track-object contact generation and crashes remain incomplete. Wheels still render in their bind pose; rider blending, race systems and progression are not finished.
entries.caption: Original hull connected to the Rust terrain-contact solver, with original sky and scene textures visible.

entries.title: Original ATV suspension moves with driving
entries.summary: The original ATV model now reflects recovered steering and suspension motion as it drives over ENV01.
details: Recovered the visual update order and original wheel-linkage transforms, then connected them to the Rust vehicle simulation; 27 mechanical nodes now move with steering, suspension compression and wheel rotation.

An original-instruction interpreter compared 100 deterministic poses across all 27 node matrices, with maximum absolute difference below 0.00000056. The public-browser regression passed with four wheels grounded and no JavaScript or WebGL errors.
entries.limitation: The instruction comparison is a finite-f32 interpreter, not PS2 hardware validation; host trigonometry differs slightly. The rider still uses a sampled seated pose, and original camera behavior, track-object collisions, crash behavior and race flow remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Recovered ATV steering and suspension parts move during a real-disc browser driving run; the rider remains in a seated pose.

entries.title: Original chase camera and static obstacle contacts
entries.summary: The browser now follows the recovered single-player chase camera and loads original static track collision meshes into the vehicle contact path.
details: The original follow-camera preset data and update behavior run in Rust. Camera button, C key and controller input cycle camera views; the combined real-disc regression exercised five views and recovered widescreen framing.

Static type-0 obstacle geometry is connected to the recovered ray-bundle query path: the browser loaded 176 collision placements, 31 meshes and 41 actor rays. Instruction-interpreter comparisons and a synthetic wall response test validate component contact behavior.
The same browser run retained the moving 27-node ATV linkage, original track scene, soundtrack and engine samples, with no WebGL or JavaScript errors and no off-origin game-data requests.
entries.limitation: Obstacle ordering still follows authored placement order; moving and compound collision types, crash/wreck behavior and camera clearance against objects remain incomplete. The rider remains a sampled seated pose. Races and full-game replay equivalence are unverified.
entries.caption: Recovered single-player chase camera, original ENV01 scene, and animated ATV linkages in the real-disc browser build.

entries.title: The local build no longer starts at a disc picker
entries.summary: A same-origin runtime manifest now takes the local build straight into the recovered ENV01 scene. The game logic remains our Rust/WebAssembly port; the manifest supplies only the original runtime files it needs.
details: The old first step asked visitors to provide a disc image before anything happened. Separating the authored port from its runtime data lets this development build start directly in the scene. The desktop and 390px mobile captures show terrain, sky, props, ATV and rider loaded without a picker.

The audio archive is much larger than the runtime set: packaging selects 21 engine samples into roughly 400 KB from a 29 MB source archive. The 21-song catalog streams in 1 MiB chunks instead of placing a full track in memory.

Local browser diagnostics recorded no JavaScript or WebGL errors; the desktop run streamed music with zero underruns, and mobile layout stayed within 390px. Runtime requests were same-origin manifest/content requests.
entries.limitation: Host-only checkpoint: the public Site still needs a release and verification of no-disc startup plus manifest requests. The browser runs authored Rust/WebAssembly, not an emulator or the disc executable. This remains a partial driving reconstruction; the rider is still a sampled seated pose, while dynamic collision, crashes and race systems remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Local development build starts on ENV01 from the runtime manifest; no disc-selection screen appears.

entries.title: The rider responds to steering, lean and reverse
entries.summary: The local build now blends recovered rider motions with the ride instead of holding one seated pose. Fourteen normal riding clips are selected from filtered steering, lean and airborne state, and the rider transitions between them through pose snapshots.
details: The original controller does not simply play a riding clip on a timer: turn and lean clips are sampled from filtered inputs. Reverse follows a separate clip path and a different controller order, so it is sampled on its own.

Rust now connects the original selector to quaternion pose blending, transition snapshots/crossfades and a Head-only look overlay. A native Rust animator probe produced 1,200 finite poses across reverse, turn, lean and air states. Separately, browser diagnostics confirmed all 18 rider nodes animate in turn/turn/reverse modes with changing matrices; the full local browser regression passed.
The captures show distinct turn/lean and reverse poses in the original ENV01 scene. Crouch and look values still use constructor defaults.
entries.limitation: Local-build checkpoint; this is partial animation recovery, not full-game or PS2-hardware equivalence. Hand/foot IK, tricks, crash poses and the full event system are unfinished. Public v4 predates this rider connection, so it should not be described as available on the Site until a later release includes it.
entries.caption: Local build: the separately selected reverse motion changes the rider pose on the original ATV.

entries.title: The public game now opens directly on the track
entries.summary: Public v4 no longer asks visitors to choose a disc image. The authored Rust/WebAssembly build reads its approved runtime files from the Site manifest, then renders ENV01 in the page.
details: This fixes the first-run gap: visitors can open the public URL and get to the driving scene without supplying an ISO. In a fresh public-browser run, the same-origin manifest loaded 68 terrain textures, 64 sky tiles, 174 scene props, the ATV and rider, 21 engine samples and the 21-song catalog.

The public regression exercised throttle, braking, reset, camera cycling, controller and focus behavior, touch/cancel input and graphics-context recovery. Music played with zero underruns; diagnostics recorded no JavaScript/WebGL errors. The 390px mobile view has no disc picker and no horizontal overflow.
The public deployment record identifies main commit 76f276315650e29841cb122095654239a03cbbed. The runtime manifest and content blobs are served by the Site; the game itself is our authored WASM port.
entries.limitation: This release is still a partial driving reconstruction. The public v4 rider still uses the seated sample pose; the normal riding animation connection is a newer local checkpoint awaiting its release. Tricks, rider IK, crashes, full races and progression remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Public v4 opens straight into the original ENV01 scene without a disc-selection step; public mobile layout was checked separately.

entries.title: We found the title art and the menu data
entries.summary: A decoded title image explains what is missing from the current drive-first build: the original screens have not vanished, but recovering their files is only the first step toward rebuilding the menus.
details: The Rust PST decoder opens the original 640×448 title screen, and the main-menu background is identified as bk_mainmenu.pst. Inventory of the 59-page UI archive reveals text layouts, widget positions and control groups, with original CEL fonts and animated-menu ATM data.
The original track catalog calls ENV01 “Caribou Peak.” That gives the map-selection recovery a concrete starting point, but the browser currently connects only ENV01 as a driving scene.
entries.limitation: This image is recovered source artwork, not a screenshot of a working menu. Title/menu navigation, map selection, race HUD and the other maps are not implemented. We have identified and decoded source assets and layout records; browser UI behavior is still the next work.
entries.caption: Original 640×448 title-screen art decoded from PST; the port does not yet display a working title screen.

entries.title: The public rider now leans into the ride
entries.summary: Public v5 replaces the fixed seated sample with recovered normal riding motions. Steering, lean, air and reverse now select rider poses in the browser build.
details: A useful detail in the original controller: the normal clips are sampled from filtered steering and lean inputs, not simply played on a timer. Reverse follows a separate clip path with a different controller order. The authored Rust port now blends 14 normal clips using ordered quaternion channels, transition snapshots and the Head-only look overlay.

On public commit 0dc5c09890df6bbf8f942309558ad168b7a8857b, the browser diagnostics recorded 18 animated rider nodes and turn/turn/reverse modes; node matrices changed with controls and the renderer regression passed with no JavaScript errors. Separately, a native Rust animator probe produced 1,200 finite poses across turn, reverse, lean and air cases.
entries.limitation: This is still partial animation recovery. Crouch and look inputs use constructor defaults; hand/foot IK, tricks, crash poses, race animation and the full event system remain unfinished. The public game still has no original title/menu flow or map selector; ENV01 is the only connected driving scene.
entries.caption: Public v5 in reverse: the rider pose changes with the recovered reverse motion.

entries.title: The title screen is now part of the local route
entries.summary: The original title screen is now the first rendered screen in a connected browser route, with the Start prompt clearly placed between the logo and legal text.
details: The prompt now has clear space above the copyright lines. Pressing Start enters the recovered Main Menu in the host-only build.
entries.limitation: This capture documents the local route only. Other original title behavior, menu callbacks and game modes remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Host-only capture: the original title logo and clearly placed Start prompt.

entries.title: Single Player becomes a real menu choice
entries.summary: The reconstructed title route now reaches the Main Menu, where Single Player is highlighted and selectable.
details: This page is assembled from original layout, widget and font data rather than a screenshot placed over the renderer. It lists Single Player, Multiplayer, Training Course, Profile Editor, Hall of Fame and Options.
entries.limitation: Only the Single Player route is currently wired onward; the other visible options are not implemented game modes. This is a host-only checkpoint and preliminary input coverage, not a complete menu-system verification.
entries.caption: Host-only local UI: Main Menu assembled from recovered layouts and UI assets.

entries.title: Freestyle is now reachable from Single Player
entries.summary: The local menu route continues into the recovered Single Player page, with Freestyle leading to the environment picker.
details: The page presents Race, Freestyle, Championships and Waypoint Editor using the original text, layout positions and UI styling. The browser currently follows only the Freestyle branch.
entries.limitation: Race, championships, waypoint editing, race HUD and progression are not implemented. This is the host-only reconstruction route; it does not claim the full original single-player flow.
entries.caption: Host-only local UI: recovered Single Player options, with the Freestyle route connected.

entries.title: Freestyle reaches Caribou Peak
entries.summary: Freestyle now opens the environment picker, shows the Caribou Peak preview and connects that choice to the existing ENV01 scene.
details: This is the first local route from the recovered title screen through Single Player into a named environment. The track catalog identifies ENV01 as Caribou Peak.
We attempted Tioga next, but its original collision data contains a non-finite triangle coordinate and currently blocks that route. The failing source triangle is under investigation.
entries.limitation: Only Caribou Peak/ENV01 currently connects to driving. Other tracks and modes remain unverified or unfinished, and this browser checkpoint is host-only. Formal menu-input regression is still pending.
entries.caption: Host-only local UI: Freestyle environment picker with the Caribou Peak scene preview.

entries.title: Freestyle now connects two original environments
entries.summary: The reconstructed title route now reaches the original Freestyle environment picker, and both Caribou Peak (ENV01) and Tioga Valley (ENV02) enter a driving scene in the local browser build.
details: The full frontend check passed title → Main Menu → Single Player → Freestyle using keyboard and synthetic controller input. Start returns to the menu and pauses the Rust frame; on a 390-pixel touch viewport, selecting Caribou loads the scene and Escape returns without overflow or JavaScript errors.
The page uses decoded original menu layouts, fonts and artwork. Its map choice now changes between Caribou Peak (ENV01) and Tioga Valley (ENV02).
entries.limitation: Host-only checkpoint; public v5 still starts directly on Caribou Peak. Only two environments and the Freestyle route are connected. Other modes, original menu callbacks, race HUD and full game flow remain unfinished; this is not whole-game PS2 equivalence.
entries.caption: Host-only capture of the recovered Freestyle environment picker on Tioga Valley.

entries.title: Four degenerate Tioga faces no longer stop the map
entries.summary: Tioga Valley (ENV02)'s `ruins.col` prop collision mesh contained four NaN plane records on triangles whose vertices collapse to duplicate coordinates. Preserving the original index/tree data while skipping only those zero-area faces lets the local browser load and drive the map.
details: The affected faces are 3, 66, 70 and 84 in ruins.col. Their stored plane words and tree/triangle indices are retained; other non-finite vertices and invalid real faces continue to be rejected.
The verified route can select Tioga from the original environment picker and start driving. The frontend test also covers returning to the menu and a narrow touch layout.
entries.limitation: This is a targeted malformed-geometry recovery, not proof of complete collision equivalence or a PS2-hardware match. Public v5 does not yet include Tioga or the reconstructed menu; race flow and other environments remain incomplete.
entries.caption: Local Tioga Valley driving scene after the targeted degenerate-face handling.

entries.title: The recovered menus and Tioga Valley are now public
entries.summary: Public v6 starts at the recovered title screen, follows the original Single Player/Freestyle route, and lets visitors drive both Caribou Peak and Tioga Valley.
details: The deployed CI build is commit 989214801f4f9a3f33971d3d0c65f91c4f6d816a. A fresh public browser run passed the menu route through Tioga driving, controller input, Caribou selection on a 390-pixel viewport, and menu pause/return without JavaScript errors.
The browser runs the authored Rust/WebAssembly port and autoloads approved runtime content from the Site manifest; it does not run a disc image or emulator.
entries.limitation: This release connects the title-to-Freestyle path and two environments. Most menu callbacks, modes, maps, race HUD and the full game remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Public v6 Tioga Valley scene reached through the recovered title and Freestyle menus.

entries.title: A touchscreen release can trigger the original preload
entries.summary: The revised mobile layout maps a right-side hold/release gesture to the original lean preload. On a real Caribou ramp run, the Rust simulation armed the preload, activated it on release, and lifted all four wheels.
details: The driving toolbar keeps Pause and Camera visible. The right half of the game view is a hold/lean/release surface: hold to prepare preload, drag independently to lean, and release when the native arming flag appears. The left pad brakes on pullback, then reverses near a stop; switching forward also brakes first.

The revised Chromium test passed right-half gestures at multiple points, continuous lean while holding preload, cancellation, simultaneous left/right input, brake-to-reverse-to-forward transitions, focus/menu pause, narrow layout, and text-selection suppression on the game surface while keeping the dev log selectable.

A real WASM ramp run used browser touches without injecting vehicle state or force. Native preload became active at strength 1 after release; upward velocity measured 9.28 feet/second at arming and 25.02 feet/second during the active interval, with all four wheel contacts clear.
That measured trajectory also reflects the ramp slope and other forces; it does not isolate the preload contribution.
entries.limitation: One Caribou ramp run is verified in host Chromium; it does not establish repeatability on other terrain. Physical iOS behavior, original trick modifiers, stunt scoring, IK and crash animation remain unverified or incomplete. The pause and touch updates are not in public v6.
entries.caption: Local mobile capture: PRELOADED feedback appears after release as the quad clears the Caribou ramp.

entries.title: The pause menu now uses recovered overlay art
entries.summary: The local build now draws a pause menu from the game's original overlay resources instead of leaving the driving toolbar as the only way back to game controls.
details: The recovered [Main Menu] overlay contributes 14 panel/navigation icons and three selection stretches, with original fonts and track textures. The authored panel offers Resume, Reset ATV, Controls, Fullscreen, Dev log and Quit to Main Menu.

The local frontend check confirmed the Rust simulation freezes while paused on desktop and 390-pixel layouts with 44-pixel targets. Resume, Controls/back and Quit were tested; only Pause and Camera stay on the driving toolbar.
entries.limitation: This is a web-authored pause panel using recovered game art, not the original pause callback implementation. Other pages and original game modes remain unfinished; this local panel is not in public v6.
entries.caption: Local pause panel using recovered overlay art and selection texture over the frozen scene.

entries.title: The pause panel and touch controls reach the public build
entries.summary: Public v7 now includes the recovered-art pause panel and the redesigned touch surface alongside the title-to-Freestyle route and two environments.
details: Public commit 114e074d7b12045a02a56aac8a64be515fa54e1f passed browser checks for the original routes, Tioga and Caribou, pause/Resume/Controls, and the 390-pixel layout. The pause image uses original overlay art; its web actions are still adaptations.

The public touch test passed right-half hold/lean/release, cancel, multitouch, braking before direction changes, pause/focus, and game-only selection suppression. A separate real-input ramp test activated native preload and cleared all four wheels without injecting forces or vehicle state.
The ramp trace measured 9.29 ft/s at arming and 25.26 ft/s during the active interval. The ramp slope and other forces also affect this trajectory; it is not an isolated preload comparison.
entries.limitation: This remains a partial reconstruction: other menus/modes, stunt modifiers/scoring, race flow and many environments are unfinished. Physical iOS and Bluetooth-controller behavior are unverified.
entries.caption: Public v7 pause panel over the running scene, using recovered overlay artwork.

entries.title: A short landing page separates Play from the dev log
entries.summary: The local v8 homepage has two choices: Play opens the unchanged game at /play.html, while Dev log opens the progress journal. Plain copy explains that the game code is rebuilt in Rust instead of emulating a PlayStation 2.
details: The page contains only Play and Dev log. A small landing script supports controller navigation between the links and gamepad A to open the selected item.
The host integration check passed landing → Play → original title/menu → Tioga and pause, then landing → Dev log → Play → title; it also checked Caribou selection at 390 pixels.
Before Play, the landing route loads no WASM, game runtime or original content. Its layout fits a 390-pixel viewport.
entries.limitation: Captured and verified on the host before publication. This entry records the local v8 checkpoint; no public landing-page route test is claimed here.
entries.caption: Local v8 landing page on a narrow screen, with only Play and Dev log.

entries.title: A short front door now leads into the browser port
entries.summary: The public site opens with two clear choices: Play enters the game at /play.html, while Dev log opens the progress journal. The landing page explains that the game is rebuilt as Rust/WebAssembly code rather than run in an emulator.
details: Public v8 deployed at 2026-10-11 22:28:28 UTC from main commit b1e815162c9cc769091ee5933f2e49e4823a5e24 after CI run 38180312529. A direct request to /deployment.json returned the same commit.
The public frontend integration passed, and the public gallery served 28 entries with 26 screenshots; all images returned HTTP 200. The live gallery included the new landing captures.
The landing fits the 390-pixel mobile view and contains only Play and Dev log. Its small script supports gamepad navigation; game code and original runtime content load only after choosing Play.
entries.limitation: Only Caribou Peak and Tioga Valley are connected. Other candidate environments are blocked by unresolved asset-name and collision issues; broader maps, race flow and the full original game remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Public landing page at mobile width, with Play and Dev log as the only choices.

entries.title: Original trees now appear across six local environments
entries.summary: Fixing one filename rule made original ecosystem records usable: the resource parser now removes spaces from unquoted fields, and missing material UVs default to zero. The host build can enter and drive ENV01, ENV02, ENV03, ENV05, ENV06 and ENV07 with original trees and bushes visible.
details: The six original ESB placement lists contain 37,948, 39,641, 26,530, 14,883, 38,968 and 6,617 entries respectively. The renderer currently selects up to 1,500 nearest placements and batches them into 7–24 draw calls per map.
All six local map runs completed without JavaScript or WebGL errors. This adds four host-only routes beyond the two environments in the public build.
entries.limitation: Visibility is provisional and does not reproduce the PS2 level-of-detail rules; this does not mean every ecosystem placement is drawn at once. ENV08 was still blocked at this six-map checkpoint; a later local checkpoint records its decoder recovery. These map changes were not yet published.
entries.caption: Local ENV06 run with original trees and bushes visible around the course.

entries.title: A touch stunt gesture now accompanies a real ramp run
entries.summary: The Nac Nac animation shows the rider crossing a leg during a touch-driven Caribou ramp session.
details: The local session reached ramp takeoff without injecting vehicle state or forces; the captured browser trace has no JavaScript errors.

The Nac Nac pose animates in the air, and its held extension persists through rear-wheel ground contact. This demonstrates the gesture/animation timing in this run, not original trick scoring or chaining.
entries.limitation: This is a local control and animation check, not a complete stunt system or a public-build feature. Original scoring, trick chaining and full stunt behavior remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Local touch session: the Nac Nac gesture control during a Caribou ramp run.

entries.title: Arlington becomes the seventh local environment
entries.summary: ENV08 (Arlington) now loads and drives locally. The packed trussbridge.col collision decoder was recovered from the original signed-16-bit expansion path, removing the blocker that had kept this track out.
details: A local driving capture shows the ATV on Arlington among its original trees, shrubs and two jumps. The local route list now includes ENV01, ENV02, ENV03, ENV05, ENV06, ENV07 and ENV08.
The public build remains v8, with only Caribou Peak and Tioga Valley connected. No new environment has been published.
entries.limitation: This verifies a local map route, not PS2 rendering fidelity. Vegetation visibility is still provisional, and terrain detail/LOD quality is under investigation.
entries.caption: Local Arlington run through the recovered trail vegetation and jump obstacles.

entries.title: The terrain detail was already stored in an alpha channel
entries.summary: The answer to the close-up terrain question was not a larger model or an upscaled texture. The original scene stores a separate _d.pst detail layer; its alpha carries the snow and dirt grain. That layer now blends into the local renderer near the ATV.
details: The ENV01 height grid is 1,281 × 1,281 samples at 4.5-foot spacing. Its largest stored macrotexture is 256 × 256 pixels, with 240 useful texels across 288 feet; no finer stored terrain model was found.
The browser now uses the original detail texture with recovered world scale and near-pass modulation. Correct UV gradients also keep tile wrapping from choosing tiny mip levels at seams.
The comparison capture shows grain in close snow that was absent in the preceding local frame. No artificial texture upscale or replacement high-resolution model was used.

The completed local detail build passed the seven-map regression with original 64×64 detail textures, moving full-sample terrain patches and batched vegetation. The 390px renderer checks passed gamepad input, touch cancellation, audio-engine startup and graphics-context restoration. Menu navigation passed immediately before the terrain-only shader changes.
entries.limitation: This is a local screenshot. Original projected-coverage pass selection, distant mip behavior, fog, and geometry rounding are still not matched; this is not a full PS2 terrain LOD result.
entries.caption: Local ENV01 after connecting the original detail layer; fine snow grain appears in the near terrain.

entries.title: Unused archive records pushed the package over the hosting limit
entries.summary: Sites refused the expanded package at its 256 MiB ceiling. The browser only needed selected map placements and rider materials, so the runtime package now keeps those referenced records instead of whole unused archives.
details: Trimming ENDL and RIDER_MT reduced startup content from 77,826,915 to 33,954,399 bytes: 43,872,516 bytes (41.84 MiB) saved. All 21 music tracks and engine-manifest records are byte-for-byte unchanged; all seven full FR map archives are also unchanged.

RIDER_MT is reduced from 681 members to the 21 material/pass textures referenced by the current meshes. Each ENDL retains its common map-placement TOY. The staged package, including 31 screenshots, is 262,602,755 bytes (about 250.44 MiB).
All seven map load/driving tests passed with the compact content, along with renderer, graphics-context restore, audio, controller and touch checks.
entries.limitation: This is a validated local package pending public deployment. No public release or public verification is claimed.

entries.title: Seven maps move to a Worker with music and assets kept in R2
entries.summary: The public build now separates its small Rust/WebAssembly game app from original runtime content streamed through R2. That keeps maps and music out of the app deploy bundle and avoids a database for the current browser-only game.
details: Public Play: https://atv-offroad-fury-2.champtoday.workers.dev/ — dev log: https://atv-offroad-fury-2.champtoday.workers.dev/devlog.html. The Worker serves main commit ad605e1b589720bd9b093ae84c25a753ea65a0fc; a live /deployment.json request confirmed the same SHA. Worker version: 63ff7d3b-1f10-4976-8673-c409cd758a6e.
R2 verification checked 281 runtime, manifest and gallery objects for exact size, SHA-256 and MIME type. All 21 music tracks remain present. The currently served gallery has 34 entries and 31 PNGs.

Public seven-map test 4299 passed. Frontend test 78959 passed the landing/controller route, title/menu, map selection, Tioga driving/pause, and 390px Caribou touch flow with no JS errors or ROM prompt.
entries.limitation: This remains an incomplete reconstruction: original menu/game modes, race flow, scoring, stunt/crash coverage and terrain LOD fidelity are unfinished. GitHub automatic deployment to the Worker has not yet been verified.
entries.caption: Cloudflare-hosted ENV03 (Sonora Dunes) with recovered terrain detail and vegetation.

entries.title: A half-inch seam had hidden Freeport Harbor
entries.summary: Freeport’s terrain was not corrupt; our seam check was too strict. Two vertices on a shared border differ by only 0.03262 feet, less than half an inch. The renderer’s dense grid now chooses the height from the tile that owns each cell, while preserving the source per-tile geometry and collision data.
details: Freeport ENV04 uses a 1,025 × 1,281 grid at 4.5-foot spacing. Its scene has 356 instances and 13,816 ecosystem placements in nine batches, with 235,870 terrain triangles and no unsupported meshes.
The scene file omits the freestyle starting direction, so the route uses original TOY start settings recovered from native routine 0x002fa3c0.
The public Cloudflare build from main commit e19ec6b4c7f515e6ea3ed7c7aa97810357109f13 passed CI run 38184851978. The automatic CI-to-Worker publish completed for this release.

Public checks passed load-and-drive for all eight maps, plus the controller/menu selector, pause, and 390px touch route without a disc prompt or JavaScript/WebGL errors. Checks also matched 23 static-app hashes and 285 runtime, manifest and PNG objects by hash and MIME; the 21-song catalog remains present.
The approved screenshot was captured on the host and shows the Freeport dirt-road spawn; it is not a public-browser capture.
entries.limitation: The eight-map build is publicly verified, but this remains a partial reconstruction. The Arlington locomotive and ten-car looping path have been recovered in research but are not rendered or connected to the game. Full race flow and original terrain LOD behavior remain unfinished.
entries.caption: Host-verified Freeport Harbor spawn on the original dirt road, with recovered vegetation and terrain.

entries.title: A phone-sized map menu now works
entries.summary: The port now has a responsive Rust-drawn menu route from Single Player to Freestyle, with all eight environment choices and touch-sized controls.
details: The menu uses recovered original fonts and map imagery, while Rust handles layout, focus, drawing, and hit testing. Keyboard, controller, and touch navigation passed the host frontend regression; the portrait picker has 44-pixel-or-larger targets.

Public Cloudflare verification on commit 1e5c4fd255a4979148bdda648e010e2fbb68221b (CI 38186584449) passed the title/menu flow, keyboard and controller navigation, mobile layout, and pause. The public test reported no disc prompt or JavaScript/WebGL errors.
entries.limitation: This is an original-style reconstruction, not a pixel-exact copy: scenic menu backdrops, animated highlights, some original callbacks, other modes, and the race HUD are still unfinished.
entries.caption: Host-verified portrait map picker: Freestyle at Caribou Peak, with large Previous, Next, Back, and Ride targets.

entries.title: The camera now makes room for portrait play
entries.summary: Portrait mode uses a longer chase view and a slightly higher, wider sightline, then restores the exact landscape camera pose and field of view when the screen rotates back.
details: The host camera test passed with 35% more chase distance and a 0.12-radian upward sightline in portrait. The adjustment stays scoped to portrait instead of changing the recovered landscape view.

Public Cloudflare verification on commit 1e5c4fd255a4979148bdda648e010e2fbb68221b (CI 38186584449) confirmed the portrait framing and restoration of the native landscape camera pose and field of view after rotation.
entries.limitation: The adjustment changes camera framing only in portrait. Crash recovery and the remaining race behavior are unfinished.
entries.caption: Public Cloudflare capture: portrait chase framing shows more of the snowy course ahead of the ATV.

entries.title: Touch pullback now drives the native rider pose
entries.summary: Touch hold/release now maps to the recovered rider preload pose, and the public build changes rider matrices without applying jump force on flat ground.
details: Public Cloudflare verification on commit 1e5c4fd255a4979148bdda648e010e2fbb68221b (CI 38186584449) passed touch hold/release and rider-matrix changes, with no preload force on flat ground.

A separate host Caribou ramp trace followed held pullback through takeoff: the first observed airborne frame retained lean after ground braking cleared, with the original pitch response and no added torque. Another ramp run landed on all four wheels and resumed driving.

The persisted-page regression passed in WebKit and Chromium with synthetic pagehide/pageshow events, then resumed driving and pause controls without JavaScript or WebGL errors. Natural navigation reloaded locally, so this does not identify the cause of the earlier hover report.
entries.limitation: The held-pose screenshot is stationary and does not show a completed jump. Full flips, stunt scoring, and crash recovery remain unfinished; the earlier hover report is still unexplained.
entries.caption: Host capture of the crouched preload pose and touch marker; this stationary check does not depict a jump.

entries.title: A status board separates recovered work from live features
entries.summary: The development log now compares verified public behavior with source recovery and host-only candidates. Filters and per-feature next steps make the unfinished parts easier to sort and pick up.
details: The board covers 26 feature areas with four states: Live, Partial, Recovered Not Connected, and Needs Research. The count tiles are feature-area counts, not a game-completion percentage; expandable cards show source notes, test scope and a concrete next step.
The eight-map public baseline is identified by its full commit and CI run. The crash row records the newer host-tested candidate separately, including its remaining camera and prop/water gaps.
entries.limitation: A recovered file format or routine is not a complete decompilation or a connected feature. Crash behavior remains partial; the train, original race HUD and flow, saves, AI and terrain LOD are unfinished.
entries.caption: Host capture of the desktop feature board. Its count tiles summarize feature areas rather than percent complete; the host crash candidate is separate from the verified public baseline.

port_status.note: Counts describe feature areas, not percent completion. Recovered means source/data behavior has evidence; it does not mean the full game is decompiled or connected. Public labels refer to the stated released baseline. Host candidate work and its separate test scope are called out explicitly.
next_priorities: Verify the host-tested wreck candidate against its exact release; continue camera and rider-versus-prop/water work without conflating host tests with public results.
Connect Arlington’s recovered locomotive and ten-car route to movement, terrain contact and collisions.
Recover original race HUD, event flow, rivals, vehicle selection and save/progression behavior.
